name: Jordan Lee (demo)
description: Fictional speaker used to demonstrate session and company relationships.

name: Daniel McCarthy, E.I.T.
description: Daniel is a Sales Engineer-In-Training at PolyUnity, working at the intersection of mechanical engineering, 3D printing and healthcare. His earlier product-design work included medical simulation models, new healthcare products and replacement components for hospital teams.

name: Samuel Adeoye
description: Samuel develops software at Enaimco, where his work supports workflows for the energy industry. He studied at Memorial University and also builds independent products, including the recording tool Notable and the recipe-extraction app Rechef.

name: Nathan Greene
description: Nathan manages day-to-day IT support at SmartICE, including computer setup, software licensing, user accounts and cybersecurity awareness. A software-development graduate of Keyin College, he also has training in cloud computing, systems administration and technical support.

name: Karen Tuffaha
description: Karen leads marketing and operations at trophi.ai, working across business and consumer markets. Her background includes digital marketing, analytics and social-media tools. She also mentors early-career professionals on marketing portfolios, professional networking and communicating their work.

name: Ann Montet
description: Ann works in business development at SiftMed, helping connect customers with technology for reviewing complex medical records. She brings a background in financial services and studied at Memorial University. Her professional focus combines customer relationships with understanding the information people need to make decisions.

name: Rahaf HajAhmed
description: Rahaf leads talent programmes at techNL, connecting students and job seekers with Newfoundland and Labrador’s technology sector. A Memorial University business graduate, she has worked in emerging-talent coordination and takes part in career events and student networking, including moderating the Summit’s Up Next in Tech panel.

name: James Geneau
description: CEO, Propel. James has more than 25 years of experience helping technology, SaaS, investment and professional-services businesses grow in North America and Europe. His background includes go-to-market planning, revenue development, customer engagement and brand strategy.

summitPerspectives.heading: Revenue is only the start of validation
summitPerspectives.summary: A sale does not prove lasting product-market fit. Geneau emphasized looking at whether customers actively use the product and stay, rather than relying on annual recurring revenue alone.

name: Steph Burry
description: Steph is a Startup Coach at Propel with nearly two decades of experience helping businesses grow. Her technology-sector background includes early roles at Verafin and CoLab, where she worked on building teams and supporting companies through early growth and rapid expansion.

name: Chelsea O'Hara
description: Chelsea co-founded DCXIX, a software and hardware business working in real-time media production. Her work includes Scenecast, a broadcast toolkit for real-time 3D communication. She has pursued mechatronics studies at Memorial University and participated in its entrepreneurship programmes and pitch competitions.

name: Jacob Critch
description: AI Product Engineer, Melotech. Jacob is a St. John’s software engineer and Memorial University computer science graduate. His background includes founding-engineer roles, startup leadership and early engineering work in legal AI. At Melotech, he works on technology connecting AI with media and entertainment.

name: Kyle Hickey
description: Kyle leads coaching at Propel and works with startup founders on developing their businesses. He brings first-hand entrepreneurial experience, including selling his own company in 2019, and an MBA from Memorial University. His approach connects research with the practical problems founders face.

name: Freddie Pike
description: Freddie is a Staff Developer at CoLab and has also served as Director of Innovation and Growth at NL Eats. A Memorial University alumnus, he has contributed to technology education through mentoring with Canada Learning Code and volunteering with Digital Waves NL.

name: Hayley McLellan
description: RISE Project Coordinator, AMAL. Through AMAL’s RISE project, Hayley helps Newfoundland and Labrador employers recruit, integrate and retain newcomer talent. She develops workplace learning programmes using research, systems thinking and practical approaches to inclusion.

name: Ameerah Mallam-Hassam
description: People & Culture, Mysa. Ameerah works in recruitment, employee experience and talent development at Mysa. Her interests include practical uses of AI in workplace processes and hiring, with attention to inclusion, access and retaining human judgement in recruitment.

name: Ema Shiroma-Chao, CCDP®
description: Ema leads professional experience and insight work at techNL and is a Certified Career Development Practitioner. Her background includes advising international students at Memorial University and advocating for targeted career services. In 2025, she received the Canadian Association of College and University Student Services’ New and Emerging Professionals Award.

name: Professor Matthew Hamilton, PhD
description: Matthew is an Associate Professor of Computer Science at Memorial University, directs its Visual and Analytic Computing Lab and founded Birch Scientific. His research connects computer vision, medical-image analysis, visualization and AI. His industrial research background includes simulation, virtual environments and holographic displays.
imageAlt: Portrait of Professor Matthew Hamilton, PhD

name: Courtney Valvasori, P.Eng.
description: Courtney directs intellectual-property work at Avalon Holographics. A professional engineer and Memorial University alumna, she works where engineering development and intellectual-property protection meet. Her public professional profile and engineering outreach describe a career combining technical work with creative and strategic thinking.

name: James Millan, PhD, P.Eng.
description: James is Chief Technology Officer at Audyse Technology and a professional engineer with more than 35 years of research-and-development experience. He holds a PhD from Memorial University and has worked in marine research and technology. His professional recognition includes the Queen Elizabeth II Diamond Jubilee Medal for contributions to marine R&D.
imageAlt: Portrait of James Millan, PhD, P.Eng.

name: Libby Carew
description: Libby advises Newfoundland and Labrador innovators on intellectual property through Springboard Atlantic. She previously worked in business development at Mitacs, connecting businesses with academic researchers on applied projects. She is a graduate of Memorial University and Toronto Metropolitan University and works in English and French.

name: Eva Reddington
description: VP of Policy, Program Development and Government Relations, Mitacs. Eva leads policy, programme development and government relations at Mitacs, where she has worked since 2016 and became Vice President in July 2025. Her earlier career included international banking, insurance and entrepreneurship education in Indonesia. She holds an International MBA from Schulich, has studied adult learning at the University of Toronto, and teaches organizational behaviour at York University.

name: Tim Perron
description: Senior Advisor, Industry and Ecosystem Engagement (Atlantic), ICTC. Tim represents ICTC in industry and ecosystem engagement across Atlantic Canada. Based in Bedford, Nova Scotia, he brings more than four decades of experience in IT, business development and regional economic growth, including leadership work in Canada and abroad.

name: Mike Maguire
description: Mike is CEO and co-founder of Copsys Technologies, which develops technology for protecting infrastructure against corrosion and biofouling. A professional engineer, he brings more than three decades of engineering and innovation experience and a Memorial University background in naval architecture and ocean engineering.

name: Heather Craniford
description: Assistant Deputy Minister, Employment and Labour Market Development, Government of Newfoundland and Labrador. Heather leads employment and labour-market development work for the provincial government. Over more than 20 years in public-sector leadership, she has held roles spanning workforce training, post-secondary education, economic development and intergovernmental affairs. Her work connects policy, programmes and partnerships to participation in the workforce.

name: Elise Parsons
description: Elise supports employers and members at techNL. Her professional background spans the public and private sectors, including four years living and working in England. A Memorial University graduate, she brings an interest in connecting people and organizations to her employer-support work.

name: Chris Hickey
description: Founder & General Counsel, Navigant Law. Chris founded Navigant Law after more than 17 years at Verafin and Nasdaq, where he worked through Verafin’s growth, international expansion and acquisition. He now provides fractional general counsel and strategic advice to technology businesses on contracts, privacy, AI and data governance, product strategy and scaling.

name: Mary Jane (MJ) Leslie
description: MJ founded Chapter 3 to help companies move from early traction to sustained growth. Her background includes building and managing startups from within, with experience in technology and business development. Her consultancy works with technical businesses on strategy, market positioning and execution.

name: Amanda Harris
description: Amanda leads customer support at Airtable, working across digital services and enterprise customer needs. Her previous support and customer-experience leadership roles include Brex and Slack. Her work connects support operations with customer retention, product adoption and feedback to product teams.

name: Susan Byrd
description: Director of Customer Experience, Trudell Medical Limited. Susan brings leadership and technology-sector experience to Trudell Medical Limited’s growing St. John’s operations and AI Centre of Excellence. Her work focuses on developing teams, supporting talent and sustaining organizational growth.

name: Hasan Hai
description: Hasan leads client success for Keyin’s workforce micro-credential programmes and serves on techNL’s board. His technology-sector background spans telecommunications, SaaS sales, customer success and education technology. He has built teams and organizations across startup and post-acquisition settings, with a focus on strategy, culture and inclusion.

name: John Atkins
description: John founded JAC, a digital marketing and development agency. He began building and selling custom computers while studying behavioural neuroscience at Memorial University, then moved into web design and programming. His work brings together technology, design and an interest in how people interact with digital products.

name: Curtis Jennings
description: Curtis leads commercialization of Angler Solutions’ Model for Energy Systems Optimization (MESO), supporting the platform’s deployment and adoption. He holds a mechanical engineering degree from Memorial University and works on connecting technical capabilities with customer needs and commercial applications.

summitPerspectives.heading: Domain knowledge as a starting point
summitPerspectives.quote: we focus a lot on the physics right and so we understand how these energy systems work
summitPerspectives.summary: Jennings described how Angler Solutions’ energy-system expertise helped reveal a modelling opportunity, while software-product development required additional capabilities.

name: Sheena Fiander
description: Managing Director, DischargeHUB. Sheena leads DischargeHUB and advises Branch Innovations on healthcare solutions, drawing on more than 11 years in health-sector innovation. Her work addresses care coordination, patient transitions and service delivery across health-system stakeholders. She is a Certified Value Based Healthcare professional and is completing a Master of Technology Management at Memorial University.

summitPerspectives.heading: Service before software
summitPerspectives.quote: taking an approach of service first and then kind of product second
summitPerspectives.summary: Fiander described learning from frontline healthcare workflows and automating individual steps after the service process was understood.

name: Liam Flanagan
description: Manager, Programs and People, techNL. Liam works with technology businesses and workers at different stages of company development, from starting a business to scaling and sustaining it.

name: Sean Williams
description: Co-Founder & Brand Strategist, Dashboard Marketing Inc.. Sean has three decades of marketing experience across Canada, the United States, the United Kingdom, Australia and the Middle East. His background includes marketing leadership, brand strategy, digital and social marketing, communications, research and project management.

name: Joshua Martin
description: Joshua works in business development at Boast, with an interest in launching and developing new markets. His public work includes discussions of innovation funding and R&D tax credits, including how businesses document and position AI-related development work.

name: Stu Greenoff
description: Stu co-founded HeadCase, a Newfoundland and Labrador initiative that brings people together for conversations about mental health. His work with the organization focuses on community, peer connection and accessible events outside the clinical system.

name: Dean MacIsaac
description: Dean co-founded HeadCase and brings more than 20 years of professional experience to his work in organizational change. His public writing also addresses startup validation, customer conversations and testing an idea before committing substantial time and resources to building it.

name: Jan Mertlik
description: Co-Founder & CEO, Get Building. Jan co-founded Get Building after a decade developing technology for clients. A Memorial University computer science graduate, he now focuses on AI adoption, custom AI systems and technical training in St. John’s.

summitPerspectives.heading: A narrow first version
summitPerspectives.summary: Mertlik’s shed-planning demonstration started with a concrete problem and a small functional version, postponing branding and complex integrations. Getting the prototype online was a starting point for inspection, not proof of production readiness.

name: Ed J. Martin
description: CEO, Genesis. Ed leads Genesis, the St. John’s technology-startup incubator. He previously built a venture-backed education-technology business that was acquired by a US education company. His background also includes film, television and interactive media.

name: Michael Tiller
description: Michael is a Project Engineer at Tiller Engineering, which he joined in 2017. His work includes structural design for telecommunications, infrastructure and energy assets, alongside business development and client relationships. He brings an interest in technology and innovation to engineering practice.

name: Chelsey MacNeil
description: Chelsey founded and leads The Purposeful Group, advising organizations on community economic development and social innovation. Her work includes organizational strategy, rural development, policy design, partnerships and facilitation across multiple stakeholders, with a focus on connecting economic outcomes with community wellbeing.

name: Karen Moores
description: Karen advises the Council of Canadian Innovators on Atlantic Canada, working with technology-company leaders on regional and national policy priorities. Her background connects innovation, technology and public affairs, including work with startups, non-profits and national organizations. She is an alumna of CCI’s Innovation Governance Program.

name: Honourable Tony Wakeham
description: Premier of Newfoundland and Labrador. Born in Placentia, Tony worked in government, healthcare administration and business before entering politics, including as President and CEO of Labrador-Grenfell Health. He was elected for Stephenville–Port au Port in 2019, became Progressive Conservative leader in 2023 and was sworn in as Premier in October 2025. He has also coached basketball and led provincial and national basketball associations.

summitPerspectives.heading: Simpler government processes
summitPerspectives.summary: Wakeham favoured more coordinated access to government services and fewer repetitive administrative steps. The discussion offered a direction rather than a finished service model, rollout date or change in procurement rules.

name: Andrea King
description: Andrea is CEO of techNL, with a background spanning entrepreneurship, media and international work. She previously led State 23 Media and has launched, operated and sold a business. Her education includes a master’s in international relations and an MBA from London Business School.

summitPerspectives.heading: The people behind growth
summitPerspectives.quote: behind the numbers are real people, right?
summitPerspectives.summary: King connected technology-sector growth to individual decisions: starting a company, backing an unfamiliar idea and helping other founders.

summitPerspectives.heading: Honest feedback
summitPerspectives.quote: I welcome all of the candid, honest conversations. I think that’s the only way that we can get better, is by being honest with each other.
summitPerspectives.summary: King invited direct criticism of techNL’s priorities and practical feedback about the support local companies need.

name: Taylor Young
description: Chief Strategy Officer, CoLab AI. Taylor joined CoLab in 2017 before its first product or revenue. As the business grew from three people to more than 200, she developed its go-to-market functions and helped shape company strategy. Her work now covers corporate development, partnerships, strategic initiatives and relationships with major customers.

summitPerspectives.heading: Ownership and self-direction
summitPerspectives.quote: ownership is so critical when you’re trying to do a thousand things at once.
summitPerspectives.summary: Young described hiring people who take responsibility and giving them room to make decisions as CoLab grows.

summitPerspectives.heading: Customer problems before solutions
summitPerspectives.quote: customers tell you the problems. Then generally we show them potential solutions
summitPerspectives.summary: Young distinguished understanding a customer’s problem from asking that customer to prescribe the product. CoLab tests possible solutions with the people using them.

name: Chris Gardner
description: Chris is Chief Strategy Officer at Spellbook. His earlier technology leadership includes serving as CEO of Sequence Bio, and his background includes Y Combinator and corporate-director training. His career has spanned building technology businesses and contributing to discussions about innovation in Canada.

summitPerspectives.heading: Hiring for growth
summitPerspectives.quote: there has to be a certain amount of tolerance for chaos.
summitPerspectives.summary: Gardner emphasized comfort with ambiguity and the ability to pursue a defined outcome with limited supervision in a fast-growing company.

name: Amanda Perran
description: National Technology Sector Leader, Deloitte. Amanda is a Deloitte partner with more than 20 years of experience helping organizations use technology to advance their goals. Her leadership and strategy work emphasizes inclusion and innovation for businesses and communities.

name: Lucy Hargreaves
description: Co-Founder, CEO, Build Canada. Lucy co-founded Build Canada following work in federal politics and leadership roles at technology companies, including Patch. Her advisory experience includes sustainability and competitiveness work with the UN, OECD and large international businesses.

summitPerspectives.heading: A place to build and stay
summitPerspectives.quote: Canadians really feeling like Canada is the best place to stay and to grow and to build a business.
summitPerspectives.summary: Hargreaves described an ecosystem of capital, mentors, customers and faster decisions that could help Canadian founders grow at home. This was Build Canada’s vision, not an announced government policy.

name: Johanna Brown
description: Founder & Principal, Rivet. Johanna’s work at Rivet focuses on helping innovative businesses bring their products and ideas to market more quickly.

name: Jon King
description: Co-Founder & CEO, Milk Moovement. Jon’s background covers several parts of the dairy industry, including processing, transportation and management. He brings that supply-chain experience to his work building Milk Moovement.

summitPerspectives.heading: Keep customer feedback close to the problem
summitPerspectives.summary: King described a goal of returning a revised product view to customers within about 48 hours, while the problem was still fresh. The article presents this as a target operating approach, not proof that every product can be delivered that quickly.

name: Zach Green
description: Co-Founder & Chief AI Officer, Mysa. Zach co-founded Mysa and became its Chief AI Officer in April 2026 after serving as COO. He leads the use of AI agents across the business. A 2016 Memorial University mechanical engineering graduate, he has worked throughout the company’s operations during his career.

summitPerspectives.heading: Human judgment at both ends of an AI workflow
summitPerspectives.summary: Green described people investigating customer needs and writing specifications, AI supporting execution, and people returning to validate, integrate, test and release the result.

name: Phil O'Brien
description: AVP - Product Development, Nasdaq Verafin. Phil’s product-development experience spans more than two decades in financial technology, cybersecurity, defence and applied research. His current interests include using AI to detect and combat financial crime.

summitPerspectives.heading: A prototype still needs a path to production
summitPerspectives.summary: O’Brien emphasized that integrations, deployment, maintenance and testing remain demanding even when AI makes prototypes faster to generate.

name: Josh Quinton
description: Josh is an Investment Advisor with CIBC Wood Gundy. His financial-services background includes managing the US east-coast business of a financial-technology firm in New York, working with market data, analytics and institutional investors. He brings experience in financial markets and business leadership to his advisory work.

name: Jaxson Khan
description: CEO, Aperture AI and Senior Fellow, Munk School of Global Affairs & Public Policy. Jaxson’s work spans technology strategy and public policy, with more than a decade of experience across business, government and non-profit organizations. At Aperture AI, he advises organizations on adopting AI and other emerging technologies.

name: Sean Silcoff
description: Reporter, The Globe and Mail. Sean is a business journalist whose work includes breaking news, analysis, columns and long-form reporting. He co-authored Losing the Signal, which examines BlackBerry’s rise and decline, and has contributed research and feedback to other non-fiction books. He also moderates conference discussions and appears in broadcast and digital media.

name: Catherine McIntyre
description: Reporter, The Logic. Catherine reports on startups, venture capital, institutional investment and labour in the innovation economy for The Logic. She previously wrote for Maclean’s and Canadian Business. Her reporting on Sidewalk Labs received a 2020 SABEW Canada award; her investigation of cancer clusters in New Brunswick earned the 2014 National Magazine Award for Best New Writer.

name: Madison McLauchlan
description: Madison reports on technology and innovation for BetaKit from Montréal. She works in English and French, covering the people and businesses shaping Canada’s technology sector.

name: Adam Walsh
description: Adam is a CBC journalist and host-producer of The Signal, Newfoundland and Labrador’s provincial lunch-hour radio programme. His experience spans radio, television and digital reporting, including an earlier assignment with Japan’s public broadcaster NHK in Tokyo.

name: Aswinkumar Rajendiran
description: Aswinkumar co-founded and leads Measure, the billing and revenue-automation business previously known as Maple. His background includes more than a decade in software development and entrepreneurship. His company works on connecting contracts, billing and revenue processes for SaaS businesses.

summitPerspectives.heading: Revenue data defines Measure's boundaries
summitPerspectives.summary: Rajendiran said Measure serves workflows across sales and finance when they share revenue data, but rejects unrelated features that dilute the product's purpose.

summitPerspectives.heading: Building is not the same as distribution
summitPerspectives.summary: AI can make features cheaper to produce without solving who will buy, why they will switch or how the company will reach them.

summitPerspectives.heading: Overcome buyer inertia
summitPerspectives.summary: He emphasized that a new solution must be meaningfully better than the existing approach for customers to accept the disruption of changing systems.

name: Carlos Coelho
description: Carlos leads sales and marketing at Boast, drawing on more than two decades in technology-sector growth and business development. His experience covers advertising, marketing and sales in Canada, the United States and Brazil. At Boast, his work connects businesses with R&D tax-credit support.

summitPerspectives.heading: Specialization makes service dependable
summitPerspectives.summary: Coelho described Boast's decision to prioritize SR&ED tax credits over general grant services to retain expertise and reliable processes.

summitPerspectives.heading: Technical specialists remain important despite automation
summitPerspectives.summary: Automated evidence collection helps prepare claims, but expert humans must still understand the underlying work and explain its technical uncertainty during reviews.

summitPerspectives.heading: Trust must justify switching providers
summitPerspectives.summary: Coelho said customers making consequential claims need to see a substantial advantage and feel confident in the service before replacing an established provider.

name: Nick Warren
description: Nick co-founded GroundControl, which develops AI software for regulated manufacturing. He previously co-founded inspectAR, later acquired by Cadence. His work brings startup experience to the practical problem of preparing and managing complex manufacturing quality documentation.

summitPerspectives.heading: Build for a repeatable customer need
summitPerspectives.summary: GroundControl declines one-off software requests that solve a problem for only one client; Warren looks for enough shared demand to support a reusable product.

summitPerspectives.heading: Expand along connected manufacturing workflows
summitPerspectives.summary: Warren described growing from generating inspection documentation toward reviewing that documentation elsewhere in the supply chain, while keeping regulated contract manufacturers as the core market.

summitPerspectives.heading: Founder-problem fit matters
summitPerspectives.summary: For an early startup, Warren encouraged founders to ask what particular advantage makes their team well suited to solve the chosen problem.

name: Jacquelyn Holden
description: Jacquelyn is a consultant focused on sales processes and leadership. Her public professional writing explores sales forecasting, the role of conversation in sales technology and the challenges of moving opportunities beyond product demonstrations.

name: Tom Snyder
description: Founder, Funnel Clarity. Tom previously led Huthwaite as CEO. His sales-leadership work examines how human behaviour affects selling and business results.

summitPerspectives.heading: Help customers discover rather than simply tell
summitPerspectives.summary: Snyder argued that buyers place more weight on conclusions they reach themselves and information they request than on unsolicited seller claims.

summitPerspectives.heading: Three ways to provide value before a sale
summitPerspectives.summary: He recommended exposing an underestimated problem, revealing an unanticipated solution or connecting the customer with helpful expertise—not immediately pushing a demonstration.

summitPerspectives.heading: Measure the buyer's decision, not seller activity
summitPerspectives.summary: Snyder proposed four evidence tests covering whether an opportunity exists, a provider can compete and win, and the promised value can be delivered. He recommended using AI for preparation without replacing human customer contact.

name: Sarah Murphy
description: Partner, Pelorus Venture Capital Ltd.. Sarah has worked with early-stage technology businesses as both a founder and operator, including Harbr.com and a construction-technology venture she co-founded. She previously served as an Entrepreneur-in-Residence at Propel and mentors through Creative Destruction Lab. She also co-authored the Gender Diversity Playbook for startups.

name: Shelley Kuipers
description: Co-Founder, CEO and General Partner, The51. Shelley co-founded The51 and leads the organization as CEO, alongside her role as a General Partner of its venture funds. Her investment work centres on women-led capital, early-stage founders and markets that have received relatively little traditional venture funding.

name: Eric Laflamme
description: Managing Director, Innovation Banking Quebec and Eastern Canada Region, CIBC Innovation Banking. Eric has more than 25 years of experience across technology delivery, management and financing. He joined CIBC Innovation Banking in 2018 to build its Eastern Canadian technology and life-sciences financing practice. He holds degrees from UQAM and HEC Montréal, participated in the 2015 Governor General’s Canadian Leadership Conference, and has served on education-related boards.

name: Brian Whiteway, MBA, CPA, FCPA
description: Brian is Senior Director of Growth & Transition Capital at BDC Capital. His background includes more than 25 years in technology leadership, alongside investing and mentoring in software and hardware businesses. His work connects growing companies with financing suited to their stage of development.
imageAlt: Portrait of Brian Whiteway, MBA, CPA, FCPA

name: Falon O'Keefe
description: Falon leads sales at Virtual Marine, developing markets for simulation technology in marine, defence and offshore energy. Her background includes commercialization, market expansion and complex procurement. She works with customers in North America and internationally and serves on techNL’s board.

name: Emad Rizkalla
description: Founder and CEO, Bluedrop ISM. Emad co-founded the business that preceded Bluedrop in 1992 while studying engineering. His entrepreneurial and speaking work explores the relationship between technology, learning and workforce development. The published biography also notes recognition in Canada’s Top 40 Under 40.

name: Joe Teo
description: CEO, HeyOrca. Joe’s experience running a small social-media agency shaped the development of HeyOrca. He and his team built the product around the collaboration, content planning and reporting needs of smaller agencies, businesses and non-profits.

name: Gerard Duggan, ICD.D
description: VP, Marketing, eGovernment & Enterprise, Vision33. Gerard has worked in IT services and digital transformation for more than 25 years, serving public- and private-sector organizations. His experience includes business development, complex technology initiatives and leading multidisciplinary delivery teams.

name: Josh Taylor
description: Founder and CEO, Carrick. Josh founded Carrick, previously called TxtSquad, to help healthcare teams communicate with patients. The platform brings several forms of patient communication and scheduling into a shared conversation.

name: Maurice Tuff
description: Maurice is a technology entrepreneur and investor with a background in new-product development and commercialization. His public professional profile lists engineering qualifications and study at London Business School. He brings experience developing technology businesses to the Summit’s discussion of growth beyond venture capital.

name: Kristen Marumoto
description: Kristen manages programmes at Genesis, supporting startup founders and the organization’s residency work. Her background includes the Memorial Centre for Entrepreneurship and work with the wearable-technology startup PUSH. She also co-founded Insights to Markets, drawing on experience helping entrepreneurs navigate early business development.
